newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to fine two firms for dangerous air cargo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to fine two firms for dangerous air cargo.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration said on Friday it would fine two Louisiana companies for mishandling hazardous materials to be shipped on cargo-carrying passenger planes.
The FAA said in a statement it would fine Stark Sales, of Bell Gardens, Louisiana, $82,500 for improperly packaging, marking and labeling five boxes containing flammable resin solution.

It said Stark knew the material was not prepared in accordance with FAA hazardous material requirements. The required emergency response information did not accompany the hazardous material, it added.
The agency also said it would fine Longfield Inspection, of Sulphur, Louisiana, $62,500 for the alleged mislabeling and mishandling of acid-filled batteries.
It said the shipment did not carry the necessary emergency response information.
